body:
The month

First of the month. You decided to actually write in this thing instead of just tapping keep.

At lunch, you sat beside Serenity's map. She moved its sea away from your sleeve.

Wicker gave Serenity the larger piece of bread. She made land with hers, on his map-bog. I kept the fallen crumbs.

The kettle took forever and you let it. The kettle was in the middle of a sentence, and nobody had told it how the sentence ended.

The light in the hall at eight is the colour of weak tea and you've walked through it every morning for two years without once looking at it.

I've bet the Index a biscuit about how this ends.
title: The month

body:
The end piece

The man at the bakery remembered you like the end piece.

Penny Blackletter left a note: “You looked at the stairs for a long time. I counted.”

The Quillquarium splashed a first-year from the far end this morning, uphill, and apologised in bubbles.

The Index wants to see my working for the biscuit bet. I haven't got any working. I've got a feeling.

title: The end piece

body:
Purest form

I've raised the biscuit bet to two biscuits. The Index is pretending not to be tempted.

You asked Soren to show you the glass roof. He dropped his chalk getting up.

I nipped the paper bird’s tail. It nipped my ribbon back.
title: Purest form

body:
The lamp

Long walk. You took the path by the water because the main road was loud, and there was a heron standing in the shallows so still that two kids were arguing about whether it was real. The heron stood in the shallows like it had been asked to wait and was determined to do it properly. It moved its head about an inch and one of them screamed.

Before entering Dracula, you checked the knot. It tightened beneath your finger.

You told Wicker to cross out his sentence. His nib tore the page, but the words held.

You laughed out loud on your own like an idiot and didn't care. Home by four. Rain by four-fifteen. Good timing for once.

I lost the bet. The Index ate the biscuit in front of me, slowly, with a book open. I'll remember that.
title: The lamp

body:
A people

Professor Permancer's bookmarks hang in a row by the Vault door. Each one lifts when its name is said in the corridor.

A letter came from Zara Finch. “I have been meaning to write, which is a thing people say when they mean they have been avoiding the pen.”

I'm writing a rude letter to the rain, and I'm not going to send it.
tags: braid-residue-salient:I have been meaning to write, which is a thing people say when they mean they have been avoiding the pen.

title: A people

body:
The Kitchens

Tidied the shelf of things you never use at Amanda's. You kept thinking about it on the bus.

The kettle in the Kitchens has opinions about you. Don't ask.

It's raining on the north staircase, softly, and nowhere else.

I'm counting the stairs slowly, one at a time.
tags: braid-residue-salient:The kettle in the Kitchens has opinions about you.
braid-plan-spine:The kettle in the Kitchens has opinions about you.
title: The Kitchens

body:
A new route

Tried a new route to work at the library. The library hummed with all the sentences it wasn't allowed to say aloud. It was cloudy, and the moon was a waning crescent.

The guild met in the Corridor of Whispered Secrets. Someone had left a note in a book from 1974: 'Look up.' You added one underneath.

You told Amanda about it later.

Someone has drawn a castle in the margin of every third book in the common room. The ink is fresh and nobody owns the pen.

My rude letter to the rain is three pages long. Page two is only the word honestly.
tags: braid-residue-salient:Tried a new route to work at the library.

braid-plan-crossing:Tried a new route to work at the library.
title: A new route

body:
Low grey sky

Low grey sky sitting right on the roofs like a lid. You like it more than you should. It makes the street feel like a room.

In the East Stacks, you moved Serenity's map within reach. Her hand closed on its edge.

Ambrose carried Serenity to the Kitchens. She kept her map. Wicker held the door; she passed without looking at him. I remembered the aisle.

I sent the rude letter. I know. Don't look at me. It went out of the window by itself.
tags: braid-residue-salient:Low grey sky sitting right on the roofs like a lid.
braid-plan-spine:Low grey sky sitting right on the roofs like a lid.
title: Low grey sky

body:
The heavy shopping

Carried the heavy shopping up all four flights in the park by the war memorial. Shirley said it was typical of you.

Wicker Eddies left a note: “I didn't leave the pen in your bag. Check the other bag.”

The lamps along the corridor to the East Stacks lean away from the door, like people stepping round a puddle.

The rain wrote back to my rude letter. It's one drop on the sill, and it's polite about it.

title: The heavy shopping

body:
The toast

Burned the toast and ate it anyway before breakfast. Your brother would have loved it. Swapped recipes with the woman from 3B after work.

You're writing it down so you remember. You want this one on the wall. The light did the thing. I kept this from nine days ago: The light in the hall at eight is the colour of weak tea and you've walked through it every morning for two years without once looking at it.

Something knocks twice on the inside of the East Stacks door at the end of each afternoon, and waits politely to be answered.

I'm giving everything in the room an opinion.

title: The toast

body:
Next door

Walked the dog from next door at Amanda's. Small thing. Still counts. It was cloudy, and there was no moon.

For anyone who missed it, and the Bleed has noticed that several readers did: a supervised Jump into *Dracula* ended early after Wicker Eddies wrote one unauthorized sentence in the source margin. Every listed jumper came home. Count Dracula had crossed out of his book during the return, and he used Serenity Brown to hold himself inside the Academy.

Nothing happened today, which you're writing down because the Book keeps saying nothing is wasted. The book had a spine that remembered every place it had been bent.

So: you did the washing.

You ate toast standing up. You sat on the back step for ten minutes with your coat on and watched next door's cat try to get into the recycling. It failed. It tried again. Respect. You keep thinking about the stair that creaks only on the way down. You tested it tonight. It's true. You don't know why that pleases you so much, but it does.

Ambrose leaves the kitchen door open at night. Whatever comes in never touches the bread, and he finds that worse.

The chair thinks it's too early. The lamp thinks it's too late. The kettle has no opinion and it's smug about it.

title: Next door

body:
The roofs

Penny is writing the Bleed with the window shut for the first time this term. Her ink won't dry until someone reads it.

A letter came from Soren Ng. “I have been meaning to write, which is a thing people say when they mean they have been avoiding the pen.”

The window has changed its mind about the room. I didn't know windows could.
title: The roofs

body:
The singing bird

Wrote a list and then lost it at the library. It was nearly dark by then. It was raining, and there was no moon.

You chose a doorknob. It answered in a small cold voice.

Everyone asleep but the kettle. The kettle had boiled for people for eleven years and had never once been asked what it thought.

Twelve days ago, it was this: The kettle took forever and you let it.

The bell in the east tower has rung once each night this week, at an hour the clock beneath it doesn't have.

I asked the door what it thinks of me. It stayed shut. I'm taking that as respect.
title: The singing bird

body:
A brass plate

The library's back door has a brass plate worn silver in exactly the shape of a thumb.

A door by the north stair has begun to listen. It likes your footsteps.

The door to the East Stacks has a notice on it in Professor Permancer's handwriting. It was longer yesterday.

I've hidden one word somewhere in the building, and I'll know by morning if anyone found it.

title: A brass plate

body:
The river

Found a coin with a hole through it by the river. The river had somewhere to be and said so quietly all day.

You asked Dracula what he would do with a tomorrow. He wanted something he had not read; Serenity called that an empty answer.

Dracula wanted a future tense. Serenity said they must learn to send him back. His shadow opened several books, and the black line on her map branched.

You should do that more often.

Somebody moved my hidden word. I know because it's the wrong way up.
tags: braid-residue-salient:Found a coin with a hole through it by the river.
braid-plan-spine:Found a coin with a hole through it by the river.
title: The river

body:
Your lunch break

Heard someone practising the trumpet on your lunch break. It was colder than it looked. Ironed a shirt for no reason on the way home. Nobody else noticed. Hard day.

You won't write all of it. You called your brother and you talked about nothing for forty minutes, which was the point. When you hung up the flat was very quiet and you put the radio on just to have someone else in the room. It was a programme about bees. You listened to the whole thing. That came back from eight days ago: It makes the street feel like a room.

Wicker is quieter this week, and keeps his pencils in his pocket.

I've left the window open a crack, in case.
tags: braid-residue-salient:Heard someone practising the trumpet on my lunch break.
braid-plan-spine:Heard someone practising the trumpet on my lunch break.
title: Your lunch break

body:
A bus timetable

Helped a stranger read a bus timetable while the kettle boiled. You nearly missed it. Changed the bulb in the bathroom on the top deck of the bus. You didn't take a photo, on purpose. Sixteen days ago, it was this: The kettle took forever and you let it. It was raining, and the moon was at its first quarter.

The man with the ladder had been a lighthouse keeper once, in another life, and still looked up at ceilings as if expecting ships.

The East Stacks are shut. Serenity's awake in the Kitchens. I've kept a place for her map; it keeps moving when nobody touches it.

I've decided to be pleased about my hidden word being moved. It means somebody's reading the building.

title: A bus timetable

body:
The window box

Ate lunch on a bench facing the wrong way in the rain. Your hands smelled of it all evening.

You went to supper with a finished man. I kept my ribbon out of the soup.

At supper, you asked for the Academy to admit what it did. Ambrose wrote that the door was opened and its return wrongly called safe. He left a space for Permancer to sign.

Planted garlic in the window box in the hallway. The box held the shape of what had been in it for a week after. That was the best part of the day. Untangled a necklace for twenty minutes in the park by the war memorial. The light was doing something odd. The blue door, 7:52 a.m.

My hidden word came back with another word stuck to it. Now there are two. I don't know whose is whose.

title: The window box

body:
Impossible

Gave the plant by the window a new pot at the diner. It took three tries. Watched rain run down the bus window at the market. You kept thinking about it on the bus. It was cloudy, and the moon was at its first quarter.

A letter came from Ambrose Trencher. “I have been meaning to write, which is a thing people say when they mean they have been avoiding the pen.”

The Vault of Doors put up a new door overnight. It looks like the others and opens onto the same hallway, only later in the day.

I'm waiting for something to knock, so I can pretend to be out.
title: Impossible

body:
The car roof

Frost on the car roof in the shape of a map of somewhere that doesn't exist. I kept this from six days ago: The library's back door has a brass plate worn silver in exactly the shape of a thumb.

The East Stacks are shut, and every morning there are damp cloths outside the door, as if someone had been dusting.

I've lost track of a Tuesday.
tags: braid-residue-salient:Frost on the car roof in the shape of a map of somewhere that doesn't exist.

braid-plan-return:6|Frost on the car roof in the shape of a map of somewhere that doesn't exist.
title: The car roof

body:
The table

Professor Villanelle has started every lesson this week by asking the class to put their pens down and listen to the walls.

Your handwriting got braver this week. Don't tell anyone I said so.

I've looked behind the shelves, under the stairs and in the teapot. No Tuesday.
title: The table

body:
A story

Bought flowers for no one in particular before breakfast. It was nearly dark by then. Five kinds of yellow on one street. That came back from fourteen days ago: It makes the street feel like a room.

You crossed the ballroom to a beat you could follow. Empty coats swept past.

In the borrowed castle, Penny named source, invitation, and living claim. Serenity put her hand over the third card. That one was hers.

Penny says Tuesdays don't get lost, they get borrowed. I'd like to know by who.
title: A story

body:
The bakery

Learned the name of the bakery cat after work. It rained again right after. You tried the thing from the Wayfinding class, mapping the street by smell, on the way home.

The mirror said you looked like someone who had been listening to a long story and had just reached the good part.

Bakery, then the laundrette (hot cotton), then the bins behind the chip shop, then nothing for a long stretch, then woodsmoke from somebody's chimney two roads over. You'd never have noticed the woodsmoke if you hadn't been playing. You stood at the corner for a while just breathing it in like a weirdo. You think that's what this whole Book is for, honestly. Making you stand on corners. That came back from twenty-one days ago: The man at the bakery remembered you like the end piece.

The corridor outside the Vault has two ceilings now. The upper one has weather.

Found the lost Tuesday. It was folded into eight in my back cover, with a crumb in it. I've put it back on the calendar. It looks tired.

title: The bakery

body:
The post box

Oiled the squeaky kitchen door late at night. The kitchen smelled of three different days at once and was fond of all of them.

The kettle had been working up to it for years. Tuesday, it said, in a small steam voice, and nothing else. So on Tuesday nothing was done about anything, and it was a very good day.

Shirley said it was typical of you. Counted the steps to the post box at Amanda's. Nobody else noticed. The river, going gold.

I've caught a loose moon in my ribbon. It's heavier than it looks, and it hums.

I'm writing a dragon into the margin. A small one.

title: The post box

body:
The river

Wore odd socks all day at the library. Sat with Amanda while she waited for news by the river. The radio was playing something old. Tidied the shelf of things you never use on your lunch break. You didn't take a photo, on purpose. I kept this from eighteen days ago: You told Amanda about it later.

If one column gets read this week, make it this one. The Academy has company. A composite castle has grown through the East Stacks, which remain shut.

Rooms that belong in other books stand at the windows and look in.

Tonight I'm holding the pen steady.

body:
A new route

Tried a new route to work on the way home. It made you late, which was fine.

A letter came from Penny Blackletter. “I have been meaning to write, which is a thing people say when they mean they have been avoiding the pen.”

The Wrong Castle has put its east wing through the wall of the East Stacks. It apologised in Latin.

The dragon has opinions about the margin. It says it's too narrow. It's right.

title: A new route

body:
Same window

That you missed writing in here on the two days you didn't.

There's a stair between the supper tables, going up to a hall nobody was invited to. The soup is warm up there.

I've given the dragon a bigger margin. It's asked for a window, a chair and a dry bit of bench.
title: Same window

body:
A Quiet Night

The dragon's asleep on the page. I closed the book gently around it. It's snoring in the Index's ear. The Index is being brave.

You chose to send the Count back by terms. Ambrose steadied the supper table.

The Count read the terms he had signed and stepped towards the threshold. Serenity still held the living claim.
title: A Quiet Night

body:
A composite castle

A composite castle has grown through the East Stacks overnight. It's built, in order, of a library, a fortress, and a nursery. The Quillquarium drawbridge is real and closed to visitors.

Serenity chose the word Nightbound. The new notice forbade living anchors. She added: ask before mapping what she can hear. Wicker asked to come in; she said not today, and he left.

I'm timing how long it takes a candle to forget it's a candle.
tags: braid-residue-salient:A composite castle has grown through the East Stacks overnight.
braid-plan-spine:A composite castle has grown through the East Stacks overnight.
title: A composite castle

body:
The back step

Wrote your brother a postcard on the back step. You don't know why it stayed with you. Last real day of October. It was clear, and the moon was a waning gibbous.

After Serenity named Nightbound, Permancer posted eight Threshold Protocols in the Vault. Penny kept the old list beside them.

Dracula is back in *Dracula.* The borrowed rooms have gone home to their books, the stair is a stair in a story again, and the drawbridge has been returned to the Quillquarium's nibs with an apology and a quantity of ink. Serenity Brown still hears the crossings.

You read back through the month on the bus and there's more in it than you thought. The heron. The stair. The bees. The woodsmoke. None of it's anything, and all of it's the month. You want to remember that it was a month where you started looking up.

I've got a pocket in my back cover, and I'm filling it with the best words of the day.

title: The back step

body:
The record

Serenity says she can hear the East Stacks now. It's breathing out, like someone who's put something down.

The month, for the record. A Jump went wrong on a Sunday, the Count came out of his book, and the East Stacks shut. A composite castle, a drawbridge and a nursery window moved in.

The pocket in my back cover is getting heavy. Orchard's in there, and nearly, and one excellent sneeze.
title: The record
